mekki-muskil:1-1.t: His saying, the Exalted: (هل أتى على الإنسان): it is said that (هل) means (قد) "indeed". The better view is that (هل) is in its proper sense, the interrogative whose meaning is affirmation (taqrīr). It is only an affirmation addressed to whoever denies the resurrection: he cannot but say "Yes, a long stretch of time has passed in which there was no man." Then it is said to him: "Who brought him into being after he was not, and gave him existence after his non-existence? How then could his resurrection and his revival after his death be impossible for Him?" This is the meaning of His saying (ولقد علمتم النشأة الأولى فلولا تذكرون), i.e. "why then do you not remember", so that you know that whoever originated a thing after it was not, without a prior model, is able to restore it after its non-existence and its death.

mekki-muskil:3-3.t:
His saying (إما شاكرا وإما كفورا): two ḥāls (circumstantials) from the hāʾ. (سميع) and (بصير) — [(بصير)] is a naʿt (adjective) of (سميع) [Translator's note: so in the source]. (إما) is for choice (takhyīr), in its proper sense. The meaning of choice is that Allah informed us that He chose a people for felicity and a people for misery; so the meaning is that He creates him either felicitous or miserable. This is among the clearest indications that Allah the Exalted has decreed all things, and created a people for felicity, who do its deeds, and a people for misery, who do its deeds. So the choice is an announcement from Allah the Exalted that He chooses what He wills and does what He wills, making whom He wills grateful and whom He wills a disbeliever; the choice does not belong to man. It is also said that it is an anticipated ḥāl (ḥāl muqaddara), the implied form being: either gratitude arises from him when he comes to understanding, which is the sign of felicity, or disbelief arises from him, which is the sign of misery; and all of that is according to what preceded in Allah the Exalted's knowledge concerning them. The Kufans allowed (ما) to be redundant (zāʾida) and (إن) to be conditional. This is not permissible according to the Basrans, because the conditional (إن) does not enter upon nouns, since nouns are not made to carry a condition, unless you imply a verb after (إن), in which case it is permissible, as in His saying, the Exalted: (وإن أحد من المشركين): "asks you for protection" (استجارك) is implied after (إن), and the second (استجارك) indicates it, so its omission is good. Implying a verb after (إن) is not possible here, because it would entail the nominative of (شاكر) and (كفور) by that verb; moreover, there is nothing in the speech indicating the implied verb. It is also said that in the verse there is a placing forward and back, the implied form being: "We created man from a mingled drop, testing him, either grateful or ungrateful, and made him hearing and seeing"; on this view they are two ḥāls from (الإنسان). This is a good view, so there is no choice for man in himself.
His saying (سلاسلا) and (قواريرا): the origin of all of it is to be a diptote, because it is a plural, and the plural is heavy; and because it is not pluralised further, so it differs from the other plurals; and because it has no counterpart among singulars; and because it is the utmost of plurals, since it is not pluralised further; so it is heavy and is a diptote. As for those readers who made it fully declinable, it is a dialect of some Arabs: al-Kisāʾī reported that they make fully declinable everything that is a diptote except (أفعل منك) "more ... than you". Al-Akhfash said: we heard from the Arabs some who make this and all diptotes fully declinable. It is also said that he made it declinable only because it occurs in the Muṣḥaf with an alif, so he made it declinable in following the script of the Muṣḥaf; and it was written in the Muṣḥaf with an alif only because they are verse endings, so they resemble rhymes and verse-end pauses, to which an alif is added for the pause. It is also said that he made it declinable only because it is a plural like the other plurals, which some Arabs pluralised like a singular, so it is declinable just as the singular is declinable. Do you not see the saying of the Prophet ﷺ to Ḥafṣa: «إنكن لأنتن صواحبات يوسف» ("You women are indeed the companions of Joseph"), where he pluralised (صواحب) with alif and tāʾ as the singular is pluralised, so it became declinable as the singular is? Al-Akhfash reported (مواليات فلان), pluralising (موالي), so it became like the singular. The grammarians recited, of al-Farazdaq:
.. وإذا الرجال رأوا يزيد رأيتهم ... خضع الرقاب نواكس الأبصار ...
(And when men see Yazīd, you see them with necks bowed and eyes cast down.)
They transmitted it with kasra on the sīn of (نواكس), making it the plural of (نواكس) with yāʾ and nūn; the nūn was dropped because of the annexation and the yāʾ because of the meeting of two vowelless letters, and the sīn remained with kasra in pronunciation. Its being pluralised shows that it is pluralised like the other plurals, and all plurals are declinable, so this one too was made declinable on that basis.

mekki-muskil:5-6.t: His saying (مزاجها كافورا عينا): (عينا) is accusative as a badal (substitute) from (كافور). It is also said: as a badal from (كأس) according to its position; also said: as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun in (مزاجها); and also said: with an implied verb, i.e. "they drink a spring", i.e. the water of a spring, then the muḍāf was omitted. Al-Mubarrad said it is accusative with an implied "I mean" (أعني).

mekki-muskil:11-11.t: His saying (ذلك اليوم): (اليوم) is a naʿt (adjective) of (ذلك), or a badal (substitute) from it.

mekki-muskil:12-12.t: His saying (جنة وحريرا): accusative governed by (جزاهم) as a second object; the implied form is "entry into a garden and wearing of silk", then the muḍāf was omitted in both. (متكئين) is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the hāʾ and mīm in (جزاهم), and its governor is (جزى); (صبروا) does not govern it, because the patience was in this world while the reclining and the recompense are in the Hereafter. Likewise the position of (لا يرون) is also accusative as a ḥāl, like (متكئين), or as a ḥāl from the pronoun in (متكئين). It is not good for (متكئين) to be an adjective of (جنة), because that would require making overt the pronoun that is in (متكئين), since it would run as an adjective of something other than what it belongs to.

mekki-muskil:14-14.t: His saying (ودانية عليهم): (دانية) is accusative by conjunction with (جنة); it is an adjective standing in place of what it qualifies, its implied form being "and a garden near". It is also said that (دانية) is a ḥāl (circumstantial) conjoined to (متكئين) or to the position of (لا يرون). (الظلال) is nominative governed by (دانية) because it is the agent of the nearness. It has been read (ودانيا) in the masculine; it is masculine because of the separation, and it is also said: because of the masculine of the plural. It is permissible to put (دانية) in the nominative as the khabar (predicate) of (الظلال), so that (الظلال) is a mubtadaʾ (subject), and the clause is in the position of a ḥāl from the hāʾ and mīm, or from the pronoun in (متكئين) if you make (لا يرون) a ḥāl from it. (دان) is also permissible, in the nominative and masculine, as mubtadaʾ and khabar, being masculine on the grounds stated above.

mekki-muskil:17-18.t:
His saying (ويسقون فيها كأسا كان مزاجها زنجبيلا عينا): (عينا) is accusative as a badal (substitute) from (كأس), or with an implied (يسقون), i.e. "they are given to drink the water of a spring", then the muḍāf was omitted; or with an implied "I mean" (أعني).
His saying (تسمى سلسبيلا): in (تسمى) there is an implied object whose agent is not named [nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent)], referring back to (العين), and (سلسبيلا) is a second object. It is a foreign indefinite noun, which is why it is fully declinable.

mekki-muskil:20-20.t: His saying (وإذا رأيت ثم رأيت): the first (رأيت) does not pass to an object according to most of the Basrans, and (ثم) is an adverbial of place. Al-Farrāʾ and al-Akhfash said that (ثم) is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of (رأيت). Al-Farrāʾ said: its implied form is "And when you see what is there", so (ما) is the object; (ما) was omitted and (ثم) stood in its place. According to the Basrans it is not permissible to omit the relative and have its ṣila (relative clause) stand in its place.

mekki-muskil:21-21.t:
His saying (عاليهم ثياب): whoever reads it in the accusative takes it as an adverbial meaning "above them". It is also said that it is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun in (لقاهم), or from the pronoun in (جزاهم), I mean the hāʾ and mīm. (ثياب) is nominative governed by (عاليهم) if you make it a ḥāl. If you make it an adverbial, you put (ثياب) in the nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject) and (عاليهم) is the khabar (predicate), with a nominative pronoun in (عاليهم); or, if you wish, you put it in the nominative by the notion of being settled (istiqrār), with no pronoun in (عاليهم), because it then becomes like a verb placed before its agent; whereas if you put (ثياب) in the nominative as a mubtadaʾ, (عاليهم) is like a verb placed after its agent, so there is a pronoun in it. Whoever made the yāʾ in (عاليهم) vowelless put it in the nominative as a mubtadaʾ and (ثياب) as the khabar, (عالي) having the meaning of a group, as the Exalted said (سامرا تهجرون), bringing the singular form meaning the group; and likewise the Exalted said (فقطع دابر القوم), which is only "the hindmost ones (أدبار) of the people", the singular sufficing for the plural. It is also permissible for (ثياب) to be nominative by its verb[al force], because (عاليا) is an active participle; so it is a mubtadaʾ and (ثياب) is an agent standing in place of the khabar of (عاليهم). On this view (عال) is singular, not meaning the plural, as you say (قائم الزيدون) "the Zayds are standing", making it singular because it runs according to the rule of the verb that precedes, so it is singular since it has put what follows it in the nominative. This is the school of al-Akhfash. (عاليهم) is indefinite because separation is intended by it, since it has a future meaning; that is why its accusative as a ḥāl is permissible, and because it is indefinite, others than al-Akhfash disallowed putting it in the nominative as a mubtadaʾ.
His saying (خضر وإستبرق): whoever reads (خضر) in the genitive makes it a naʿt (adjective) of (سندس), and (سندس) is a collective noun; it is also said to be a plural whose singular is (سندسة); it is the fine kind of brocade. Whoever reads it in the nominative makes it a naʿt of (ثياب). Whoever reads (وإستبرق) in the nominative conjoins it to (ثياب), and whoever reads it in the genitive conjoins it to (سندس). (الإستبرق) is the thick kind of brocade. (إستبرق) is a foreign indefinite noun, which is why it is fully declinable, and its alif is a disjunctive alif (alif qaṭʿ) in foreign nouns. Ibn Muḥayṣin read it without declension, which is a mistake if he made it a noun, because it is a declinable indefinite. It is also said that, rather, he made it a past verb from (برق); this is permissible in wording but far-fetched in meaning. It is also said that in origin it is a past verb on the pattern istafʿala from (برق), so it is Arabic, from (البريق) "glitter"; when it was used as a name, its alif became disjunctive, because it is not the origin of nouns that the connective alif should enter them; it entered only into a limited number of weak nouns altered from their origin, on which no analogy is made.

mekki-muskil:23-23.t:
His saying (إنا نحن نزلنا): (نحن) is in the position of the accusative as an adjective of the noun of (إن), because a pronoun may be qualified by a pronoun, since that is in the sense of emphasis, not in the sense of description; it may not be qualified by an overt noun, because that is in the sense of description, and the pronoun has no need of description, since it is only made a pronoun after its description and identity are known; but it does need emphasis so that the predication about it may be confirmed. It is not permissible [Translator's note: so in the source; the context suggests «ويجوز» "it is permissible" was intended] for (نحن) to be a separating pronoun (fāṣila) with no position in i'rab and (نزلنا) the khabar (predicate). It is also permissible for (نحن) to be nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject) and (نزلنا) the khabar, the clause being the khabar of (إن).
And His saying (ويذرون وراءهم يوما): (وراء) means "in front of" and "before". That is permissible in (وراء) because it carries the meaning of concealment: whatever is concealed from you, whether before you, in front of you or behind you, is called (وراء) because it is concealed from you. (يوما) is an object of (يذرون). We have already mentioned the origin of (يذرون) and its explanation.

mekki-muskil:24-24.t: His saying (آثما أو كفورا): (أو) is for permission (ibāḥa), i.e. "do not obey this kind". Al-Farrāʾ said: (أو) in this is like (لا), i.e. "do not obey whoever sins nor whoever disbelieves", and that is in the sense of the permission we mentioned. It is also said that (أو) means (و) "and", but that is far-fetched.

mekki-muskil:30-30.t: His saying (وما تشاءون إلا أن يشاء الله): (أن) is in the position of the accusative as an exception, or in the position of the genitive according to al-Khalīl's view with the preposition implied, and according to the view of others in the position of the accusative since the preposition has been omitted; its implied form is "except by Allah's willing". This has many parallels that preceded: we mentioned their i'rab once according to the view of al-Khalīl and Sībawayh and once according to the view of others, for brevity, and once we mentioned both views together, as a reminder.

mekki-muskil:31-31.t: His saying (والظالمين): accusative with an implied verb, i.e. "and He punishes the wrongdoers; He has prepared for them a punishment", because preparing punishment leads to punishment; that is why implying (يعذب) is good, since the context of the speech indicates it. It is not permissible to imply (أعد), because it only passes [to this object] by a preposition; in this and what resembles it, only a verb that passes without a preposition is implied, one indicated by the context of the speech and the purport of the address. In the reading of ʿAbd Allāh [Ibn Masʿūd]: (وللظالمين أعد لهم), with the genitive lām on (الظالمين), with the implied form "and for the wrongdoers He prepared — He prepared for them". The Kufans said: (والظالمين) is accusative only because the wāw with it is an adverbial for the verb, namely (أعد); and this is speech whose meaning cannot be made out. It is permissible to put (الظالمين) in the nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), with what follows as its khabar (predicate); al-Aṣmaʿī heard someone reading so, but it is not acted upon in the Qur'an because it differs from the script of the Muṣḥaf and from the body of the readers. Al-Farrāʾ made it, in the nominative, like His saying, the Exalted: (والشعراء يتبعهم الغاوون); but it is not like it, because before (والظالمين) there is a verb that governed an object, so the clause was conjoined to a clause, and it was necessary that the [noun of the] predication in the second clause be accusative, just as it was in the first clause, in His saying (يدخل من يشاء). Before His saying (والشعراء) there is a clause consisting of mubtadaʾ and khabar, so it was necessary that the second clause be likewise. So the nominative is the proper aspect in (الشعراء), and the accusative is permissible outside the Qur'an; and the accusative is the proper aspect in (والظالمين), and the nominative is permissible outside the Qur'an. This is a principle to be relied upon in this chapter.
